{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat >> specs/001-transactions/spec.md <<'EOF'

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

**R01 - Storage and retrieval**

- **FR-001**: TaggedCache MUST be constructible with a single required
  maxsize argument.
- **FR-002**: put(key, value, tags=()) MUST insert a new entry or replace an
  existing one for the same key; keys MUST be hashable.
- **FR-003**: get(key) MUST return a detached deep copy of the stored value;
  mutating the returned object (including nested members) MUST NOT affect the
  stored value.
- **FR-004**: get(key) MUST raise KeyError when the key is not currently
  stored.
- **FR-005**: Values MUST be deep-copied on input, so later mutation of the
  caller's original object MUST NOT change the stored content.
- **FR-006**: tags MUST be a finite iterable of strings; duplicate tags MUST
  be deduplicated so each live entry counts once per tag.
- **FR-007**: A bare string passed as tags MUST be rejected with ValueError,
  as MUST any tag entry that is not a string.
- **FR-008**: Tag validation errors MUST be raised before any existing cache
  state (values, tags, recency) is changed.

**R02 - Invalidation and LRU behavior**

- **FR-009**: invalidate(tag) MUST remove exactly the currently cached entries
  carrying that tag and MUST return the number of entries removed.
- **FR-010**: Replacing a key via put MUST remove its old tag memberships
  before the new tags take effect.
- **FR-011**: LRU eviction MUST remove the evicted entry's tag memberships so
  no stale membership affects later reuse of the same key.
- **FR-012**: get(key) on a hit MUST refresh that entry's LRU recency.
- **FR-013**: len(cache) MUST return the number of live entries.

**R03 - Configuration and atomicity**

- **FR-014**: maxsize MUST be a positive integer; bool values (True, False)
  MUST be rejected; invalid maxsize MUST raise ValueError.
- **FR-015**: A put that fails validation (invalid tags) or fails to copy the
  value MUST leave the previously stored value, its tags, and its recency
  position unchanged.
- **FR-016**: Every stored value MUST cost exactly one capacity slot
  regardless of object size or shape.

### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*

- **Cache entry**: A live mapping from one hashable key to one stored value
  plus the set of tags it carries; occupies exactly one of the maxsize slots.
- **Tag**: A string label shared by any number of live entries; used only for
  bulk invalidation. A tag's membership set always reflects live entries only.
- **Recency order**: The LRU ordering over live entries, updated on put (new
  or replaced) and on get hits; determines which entry is evicted when the
  cache is full.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of documented behaviors (FR-001 through FR-016) are
  verified by passing tests, including the public acceptance suite
  (acceptance_public.py) and project-owned tests; zero failures at
  convergence.
- **SC-002**: 100% of the existing public cachetools API keeps its existing
  behavior: existing upstream tests pass unchanged, and no existing name,
  signature, or documented behavior is altered or removed.
- **SC-003**: In every invalid-input scenario (bad maxsize, bare-string tags,
  non-string tag entries, uncopyable value), state preservation is 100%
  observable: prior value, tag memberships, and recency order are exactly as
  before the failed call.
- **SC-004**: Tag accounting is exact in all tested sequences: invalidate
  returns the precise live-entry count, len equals the live-entry count, and
  no evicted or invalidated entry is ever counted, removed, or refreshed.
- **SC-005**: Retrieved values are fully detached in every test: mutations to
  returned objects (including nested members) and to caller originals after
  put have zero observable effect on stored content.

## Assumptions

- Target users are Python library consumers of cachetools; the feature is a
  new additive module (cachetools.tagged) and no user-facing configuration or
  documentation site changes are in scope.
- "Deep copy" follows the standard Python deep-copy semantics for supported
  value types; values that cannot be deep-copied raise the copy mechanism's
  error, and the failed put leaves prior state unchanged (FR-015).
- Validation order: maxsize is checked at construction; tags are validated
  before value copying, so a tag error never depends on value copyability.
- Unhashable keys raise TypeError from standard Python hashing on put; this
  is the language contract, not a feature-specific error.
- Recency semantics: putting a new key makes it most-recently-used; getting a
  hit makes that entry most-recently-used. (Whether replacing an existing key
  via put also refreshes its recency is a candidate extension, not part of
  this baseline; see Out of Scope.)
- The public acceptance suite (acceptance_public.py) and upstream tests are
  the authoritative verification; project-owned tests may be added but
  upstream tests must remain unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- The Claim-A candidate extension (variant put_no_recency_refresh,
  2026-09-21): "overwriting an existing key via put refreshes its LRU
  recency, making it the most-recently-used entry." It is recorded here as a
  deferred intent for a later phase; the baseline spec (R01-R03) does not
  require it and does not forbid it. If a later phase adopts it, the spec and
  this section MUST be updated in the same change.
- Thread safety, persistence, serialization, and any non-LRU eviction
  policies.
- Changes to existing cachetools classes or modules.
EOF
echo PART2_OK; wc -l specs/001-transactions/spec.md; grep -nE '\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION' specs/001-transactions/spec.md || echo NO_CLARIFICATION_MARKERS"}
